Mia Latter was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023
A woman who alleges that she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity and is campaigning for a staggered age of consent in an interview with the Sunday Times.
Mia Latter was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation. She was known under the pseudonym 'Alice'. Brand denied the allegations at the time.
None of the women in the 2023 media investigation were complainants in Brand's recent criminal trial.
Reacting to the proposal, Cabinet Office Minister Louise Haigh said it would be a "massive step" to change the age of consent law, but that it "deserves proper consideration and scrutiny".
Speaking to the Sunday Times, she added that it was "disgusting" that a culture existed in the 2000s that "normalised and celebrated" celebrities having relationships with teenagers.
On Monday the entertainer was sentenced to 10 and a half years for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two counts of rape and one allegation of attempted indecent assault.
The Sunday Times reported that Latter had initially described the allegation about Brand to them as a sexual assault and that is how they reported it in their 2023 investigation.
Latter, 37, "now calls this allegation rape", the paper said.
Latter said she was 16 when she met Brand, who was 30 at the time, when she was on her way home from a shopping trip. She said Brand was working at MTV.
She told the paper: "I think people were so struck by my story because of the age difference and the clear imbalance [in power]."
She said Brand told her to keep their relationship secret from her school friends and claimed that he referred to her as "the child" in front of his entourage.
It was towards the end of their relationship that Latter was allegedly orally raped by Brand, according to the Sunday Times.
Latter said that she was now campaigning for the introduction of a "staggered" age of consent that would prohibit relationships between 16- and 17-year-olds and adults.
"I don't want to criminalise teenagers having sex with each other," she told the paper. "If you're between the ages of 16 and 18, it seems reasonable that you can have relationships with each other, and [teenagers] are always going to. But … if you're in your thirties, forties and fifties and you're trying to have a relationship with someone under the age of 18, it [should be] a criminal offence."
She also told the paper that she would not continue with the criminal process so she could focus on her campaign.
In her interview with the Sunday Times she said that the CPS decided not to include her as part of Brand's criminal trial but the police wanted her to be part of a "subsequent trial".
A Met Police spokesperson said: "Officers launched an investigation in January 2026 after receiving an allegation of rape.
"Detectives sought advice from the Crown Prosecution Service to determine how best to proceed, and officers were advised that further information was needed before a charging decision could be made.
"This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence."
A spokesperson for the Crown Prosecution Service said it would "continue to work closely with investigators to provide advice and make sure cases progress as quickly as possible".

Ukraine’s NATO ambition has always been a red line for the Kremlin. Giving up territory has been a no-no for Ukraine. Will they make compromises?
The United States has pitched a new pathway for Ukraine to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), an aspiration that Kyiv has long held as a means to guarantee its defence against Russia, almost five years into their war.
But the administration of President Donald Trump has suggested that Ukraine would need to agree to give up all of the Donbas region in the country’s east, which Russian President Vladimir Putin has demanded as one of his conditions for ending the war.
The idea, according to Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, was communicated to him by Trump’s negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner at the latest round of US-mediated peace talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, last week.
After the Abu Dhabi round of talks, Kushner and Witkoff met Putin in Moscow on Thursday, then briefed Zelenskyy in Dublin, before a meeting of European leaders in the Irish capital on Friday.
Ukraine applied to become a member of NATO in September 2022, seeking to fortify its borders with Russia.
But the Kremlin has repeatedly said Ukraine becoming a member of NATO would demand “a harsh response” from Russia.
So will Washington’s latest pitch be acceptable to both Ukraine and Russia?
On Saturday, Zelenskyy told reporters that Kushner and Witkoff had suggested that Ukraine could become a NATO member if it ceded control of Donbas in the east.
He said, “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?'”
“NATO is back on the agenda” since it is part of an “extremely difficult” conversation between Ukraine and Russia which would determine the future of European security, Zelenskyy said.
Putin has been against Ukraine’s NATO membership and has demanded that the alliance pull back its troops from countries bordering Russia.
“This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations,” Zelenskyy said.
“Real security in Europe means the EU [European Union] and NATO. That’s it. There is no other security in Europe.”
Ian Lesser, distinguished fellow at the German Marshall Fund of the United States told Al Jazeera that the US proposal, if accurate, is significant because it articulates very directly an approach long current in US administration circles that Ukraine should be prepared to make territorial concessions in the service of a settlement.
“The NATO element seems very doubtful. Surely attractive to Ukraine, but [it is] hard to imagine Moscow agreeing to this. And some NATO members will be doubtful too,” he said.
Chris Featherstone, a political scientist from the University of York in the United Kingdom argued that the proposal was a major departure from previously held positions.
“The US has been very cautious about getting further involved in Ukraine, with the Biden administration giving military support, but clearly opposing any ideas of Western involvement on the ground. Trump has seemed to be very sympathetic to the Russian cause, and has had significant blow ups with Zelensky, so this proposal is certainly a surprise,” he noted.
He told Al Jazeera that offering NATO membership in a peace settlement would give significant support to Ukraine should Russia reinitiate the conflict in the future.
“In the light of Trump’s repeated attacks on NATO this could be seen as a recommitment to the alliance. However there would be questions over whether Trump could bring other NATO allies to support the proposal,” he added.
Ukraine applied to become a NATO member in September 2022, just months after Russia’s full-scale invasion of the country.
Since then, Zelenskyy, his officials and Ukrainians around the world have been lobbying NATO nations to speed up Kyiv’s accession process.
But NATO members remain divided over offering Ukraine alliance membership amid an ongoing war despite a broad consensus to signal strong support for Kyiv.
NATO members bordering Russia, like Lithuania and Poland, have been most enthusiastic about backing Ukraine’s ambitions. Several other nations in the alliance have also been supportive of an expedited process for Kyiv to join, amid concerns about corruption in Ukraine and while seeking an end to the war with Russia as a condition for the country to become a NATO member.
But under President Trump, the US has been far less receptive to Ukraine’s calls for NATO membership. Trump has publicly told Ukraine to give up on hopes of joining the alliance.
Yet, while the new proposal from Witkoff and Kushner revives Ukraine’s hopes of joining NATO, it demands a compromise that no government in Kyiv can easily make.
On Saturday, Zelenskyy told reporters that the prospect of Ukraine joining NATO in exchange for ceding territory had not been raised by members of the alliance before and reiterated that Kyiv would not give up any of its territories.
But he said if Ukraine received a peace deal which included security guarantees, the right to maintain a strong and well-funded Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild the country, then he would hold a national referendum on the question of ceding territory in exchange for NATO membership.
Featherstone noted that Ukraine has been fighting for a long time, and has consistently maintained that it will not relinquish it’s territory in a peace deal.
“The proposal from the Trump administration is clearly an attempt to test this Ukrainian position, in an effort to confront the impasse,” he said.
“NATO membership would give a level of security that Ukraine would likely welcome, however, this would be a big sacrifice of territory and sovereignty. After years of Trump’s questioning of the NATO commitment, Ukraine would need a strong statement of commitment to its defence should they be considering any proposal like this,” he added.
The Kremlin has not yet responded to the latest US proposal.
But it has maintained a strict position that Ukraine’s NATO membership is a red line for Moscow and a direct threat to Russia’s national security. In fact, Putin has also cited the issue of Ukraine’s NATO aspirations as one reason why Russia launched its war in 2022.
Despite Kushner and Witkoff’s meetings with Putin, the Kremlin has shown little appetite for a change in that position. Moscow has continued, throughout the war, to demand that Ukraine abandon its NATO ambitions and maintain a neutral and demilitarised status. Russia has also firmly opposed any deployment of Western troops or peacekeepers on Ukrainian soil.
In addition to demanding that Ukraine give up its NATO dreams, Moscow has also insisted that Ukraine should cede sovereignty over the Donbas region, in addition to parts of Zaporizhia and Kherson provinces that Russia already occupies.
Just as the new US proposal asks Ukraine to give up some territory in return for a NATO seat, it offers Russia a bargain — withdraw the red line on Ukraine’s NATO membership and get Donbas in exchange.
The region in eastern Ukraine has historically been the country’s industrial heartland and is therefore a critical economic engine.
A majority of people in the Donbas identify as ethnically Ukrainian, but a minority identifies as ethnically Russian. The Russian language is also widely spoken in the region — a legacy of Russian migration there in the 19th century and then under the Soviet Union.
Russia accuses Ukraine of discriminating against Russian-speaking and ethnically Russian people in the Donbas, and has used this claim to justify its demand that Kyiv hand over the region to Moscow.
The region consists of the provinces of Luhansk and Donetsk. Since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Russia has occupied almost all of Luhansk and most of Donetsk. In all, it controls about 88 percent of the Donbas region. But it has consistently demanded that Ukrainian troops withdraw from the remaining parts of the Donbas they cur…

Mia Latter says she was in an abusive relationship with the convicted rapist when he was 30 and she was 16
A woman who alleges she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity to campaign for a staggered age of consent.
Mia Latter says she was in an abusive three-month relationship with Brand when he was 30 and she was 16.
Previously identified using the pseudonym ‘Alice’, Latter said in an interview with the Sunday Times that she had been inspired by Gisèle Pelicot to give up her lifelong right to anonymity.
“It’s not my shame,” she said. “It’s not my burden to carry any more. It’s not me lying, and I didn’t commit any crimes.”
Latter is calling on the UK government to introduce a “staggered” consent law, which would make it illegal for adults over a certain age to have sex with 16- and 17-year-olds.
Louise Haigh, the de facto deputy prime minister, said that Latter’s “heartbreaking story” meant a law change deserved consideration.
She told the Sunday Times: “We need to listen to Mia and other victims like her who have been through these experiences because it’s really important that as lawmakers their experience is at the heart of what we consider.
“It clearly would be a massive step to change the age of consent, but it deserves proper consideration and scrutiny. I can absolutely understand why she is calling for it.”
Under UK law, adults of any age are legally able to have sex with consenting 16- and 17-year-olds.
Latter told the paper: “It’s shocking to me time and time again that whenever the news comes up again about [Brand], it’s always in the comments about the relationship with a 16-year-old.
“That’s not the most heinous bit. But why is that the thing that everybody collectively gets stuck on? I think we all sort of agree that … adults shouldn’t be allowed to have sexual relationships with children, with somebody under the age of 18. That really doesn’t seem like a gigantic leap to take.”
Latter, now 37, was 16 when she first met Brand in Leicester Square, central London, while she was on her way home from a shopping trip.
He took her number and later messaged her, asking if she wanted to go for dinner, she said.
She said that Brand – who was working at MTV at the time – still asked her to meet after she had confessed her age to him.
Latter alleges Brand orally raped her towards the end of their three-month relationship.
Brand denied all of the allegations made against him by Latter when they were first reported in 2023 by the Times.
She spoke to the police after the documentary, but the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decided not to include her case in Brand’s trial at Southwark Crown Court.
He was convicted of attacks against four of the six women who gave evidence against him, and is now serving a 10-and-a-half-year prison term for one count of rape and three sexual assaults.
Earlier this week, it was announced that a series of “serious” sex offence allegations against comedian David Walliams are being probed by the Metropolitan police after an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News.
One woman described her alleged encounter with Walliams when she was 15 as “sexual assault”.
Haigh went on to say that, in light of news that one of Walliams’s accusers was asked to sign a non-disclosure agreement (NDA), the government should also look at banning them in cases of alleged sexual assault and harassment. She said: “When we consider the allegations against David Walliams, teenagers who were fans wouldn’t come under the current consultation.
“I do think there is a very strong case to look at banning NDAs in all circumstances where they relate to harassment or discrimination, to make sure that no victim, regardless of where it happened or what their relationship was with the perpetrator, should ever be silenced.”
It is believed MPs outside Labour may support a bill to change the age of consent laws, with Jess Brown-Fuller, the Liberal Democrat justice spokesperson, coming out in favour of reviewing them.
Commending Latter for the “extraordinary bravery” it took to waive her anonymity, Brown-Fuller said: “I think we must go further to increase protections for young women and girls, and looking at a staggered age of consent is an important step.
“We already have rules that recognise power imbalances in professions: between teachers and students, or barristers and junior colleagues. It’s time for the government to recognise the implicit power imbalance held by older men over teenage girls.”
Latter’s decision to come forward was also praised by Bridget Phillipson, the minister for women and equalities, who said she “and thousands of others across the country will be in awe of her courage and determination”. She added that it is “up to all of us to send a message to women and girls who experience sexual violence: the shame is not yours. Women like Mia are leading the charge, but we can and must do more to make this a moment of change.”
Latter’s allegation was reported to the Met police, who said the investigation into the alleged rape remains ongoing.
A Met Police spokesperson said: “Officers launched an investigation in January 2026 after receiving an allegation of rape.
“Detectives sought advice from the Crown Prosecution Service to determine how best to proceed, and officers were advised that further information was needed before a charging decision could be made.
“This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence.”
The CPS said: “The Crown Prosecution Service will continue to work closely with investigators to provide advice and make sure cases progress as quickly as possible.”

Fears for national college entrance exam next week as test taker admits sending photos of questions to AI tool
The marks attained by the top scorer ⁠on South Korea’s national exam for aspiring tax accountants this year seemed too good to be true. On Sunday, sceptics were ⁠proven right when he ⁠confessed to ​using generative AI to cheat.
The scandal follows months of speculation after he scored near-perfect marks on hundreds of questions over two exams ⁠taken in April and July. It has also raised the stakes for organisers of South Korea’s annual college entrance exam this Thursday.
“I cheated using ⁠electronic devices and generative AI. My passing the exam with the top score was not ​the result of fair effort,” the candidate said, ‌identifying himself by the ‌surname Han, as he apologised on the YouTube channel Attorney Lee Don-ho.
Han, who ranked first in both rounds of the qualification exam held in April and July, confessed through his lawyer that he used AI to obtain answers during the tests. He said he had cheated by ‌taking photos of the exam questions with a microcamera, sending them to an AI tool and checking the answers on a smartphone.
His score of 397.5 out of 400 points in the first round, with only one wrong answer out of 160 questions, had sparked accusations that he cheated using smart glasses, which he initially denied.
Speaking on camera wearing a face mask, Han said he had submitted a written confession to Seoul police.
The Seoul metropolitan police agency said: “We received a written confession through the test taker’s lawyer this morning regarding cheating on the tax accountant exam,” adding that the case had been assigned to investigators.
The scandal has rattled a ‌country where standardised tests largely dictate social mobility and career trajectories. It comes just days before Thursday’s annual national college entrance exam, ‌a high-pressure event for which many South ​Korean students will have spent much of their lives preparing.
“The presidential office views ​the matter very seriously, and because the college entrance exam is next week, we have been working hard to prepare countermeasures,” a senior presidential office official told reporters on Sunday.
The official said that reports of potential cheating in the certified public accountant exam were concerning, adding ⁠that the presidential chief of staff for policy would convene an emergency meeting later ​in the afternoon to ​address the issue.
The prime minister, Han Seong-sook, acknowledged on Friday public concerns over AI-assisted cheating. The government would “prepare thoroughly in advance and closely oversee the process until the very end to ensure the college entrance exam is conducted fairly and stably”, a statement from her office said.
Reuters and Agence France-Presse contributed to this article

Joana Rosa and four other opposition candidates face off against President Jose Maria Neves, who wants a second term.
Voters have begun casting their ballots in Cape Verde, where President Jose Maria Neves is facing off against the West African island nation’s first female presidential candidate, Joana Rosa, in a vote hinging on slowing down persistent emigration.
More than 300,000 people are eligible to vote on Sunday from 8am to 6pm (09:00 GMT to 19:00 GMT) and will choose from six presidential candidates in a country known for its stability in the politically volatile region.
Neves, a member of the country’s oldest political party, the African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde (PAICV), is tipped to be the favourite but faces his strongest challenger in Rosa of the Movement for Democracy party.
The 66-year-old served as prime minister for 15 years and became president in 2021. His party won 37 of 72 parliamentary seats in May, allowing Neves to appoint Francisco Carvalho, then mayor of the capital, Praia, as prime minister.
Rosa, an opposition candidate and former justice minister, is the first woman to run for president since independence in 1975. Her party governed for 10 years before the May vote.
The country runs a hybrid parliamentary-presidential system of government that sees the president enjoy veto authority and a mediating role.
Cape Verde, a tourism haven located off the coast of Senegal, gained global fame this year after its men’s football team battled with much bigger nations to reach the World Cup knockout stages. In April, a cruise ship sailing off its coast was struck by a hantavirus outbreak.
Emigration has long been a problem because of a dearth of jobs. The archipelago has more people living in the diaspora than the 500,000 people residing on its islands. Most are in Portugal, its former coloniser, and the United States.
Nearly 77,000 diaspora Cape Verdeans are registered to vote at embassies abroad.
Neves has promised to organise a youth summit to address emigration if he is elected to a second term. Rosa, meanwhile, called for a government that allows young people “to build their futures here at home and prevent the continued exodus of young Cape Verdeans abroad”.
But many voters feel distant from the political class over concerns that it doesn’t understand their daily difficulties, Roselma Evora, a professor of political science and gender studies at the University of Cabo Verde, told The Associated Press news agency.
Candidates must clinch more than 50 percent of the vote to win, or the top two candidates will face a run-off vote on November 29.

Hundreds of thousands expected to rally against plan to scrap licence fees and fund broadcasters from state budget
Hundreds of thousands of Czechs are expected to rally in Prague on Sunday to protest against what they say is a government attempt to stifle media freedom.
The gathering to save the mandatory licence fees that fund Czechia’s public broadcasters could be one of the biggest in the nation’s history, organisers say.
It will mark the latest challenge to the prime minister, Andrej Babiš, and his coalition of populist, hard-right nationalist and Eurosceptic parties, and follows weeks of demonstrations in towns and cities and a strike by staff at Czech TV and Czech Radio.
Protesters say the plan to scrap licence fees and fund the broadcasters from the state budget would give ministers more leverage over newsrooms and follow the example of Slovakia , Hungary, Poland and Serbia, where current and previous rightwing populist governments eroded media independence.
The Million Moments for Democracy group that is organising the demonstration said the authorities would see the level of opposition. “Babiš and his government obviously think they will get away with anything … that they can ignore experts, silence critics and treat democratic institutions like their property,” it said in a statement.
The group expects 400,000 to 600,000 people at Letná Plain, which overlooks Prague’s historic centre. Some protesters would be channelling wider opposition to the government, said Daniel Stach, a TV presenter and one of the most recognised faces of the campaign.
The proposed changes, which would cut state television and radio budgets by about 15%, have drawn fire from international media organisations.
The European Broadcasting Union, the European Federation of Journalists, Reporters Without Borders and the International Press Institute have also criticised the government’s media plan and compared it to controversial moves by Slovakia’s prime minister, Robert Fico , and Hungary’s former premier, Viktor Orbán .
Babiš, a billionaire who returned to power last year, said protesters were riling up the public with unfounded claims about threats to media freedom. Last week he published an op-ed on what he called the “seven lies” being peddled by the opposition over the licence fees, which together add up to 205 koruna (£7.03) a month.
“Anyone who talks about ‘nationalisation’ [of public media] is deliberately lying,” he wrote, describing the criticism as “hysterical outbursts”. “Under no circumstances will we interfere in editorial work.”

‘We think dialogue is a good thing,’ Australian PM says after German chancellor urges the US to work with Europe for peace in Ukraine
Australia has endorsed this week’s historic summit between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in China, even as European leaders warn that the US president must not make major concessions over the war in Ukraine.
The three-way summit is planned to take place in Shenzhen, where the leaders will gather for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meeting. The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , has warned the talks must not lead to a redistribution of influence among world powers or the abandonment of his country, more than four years into the war sparked by Putin’s full-scale invasion.
Speaking in Manila on Sunday, the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese , welcomed the talks taking place but insisted the clear message to Putin was that the war should end.
Albanese, in the Philippines before a meeting of Quad leaders and talks with south-east Asian leaders at the Asean summit, left open the possibility of joining an Apec group photo with Putin if China wished for it to go ahead.
“We think that dialogue is a good thing and we await the outcome of that dialogue,” he said.
“It’s obviously quite significant, the fact that President Trump will be at Asean as well as at Apec, and that we’ll have a Quad leaders meeting as well.
“We want to see something constructive come out of that, including we want to see a de-escalation in the conflicts around the world.”
German’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz , expressed hesitation about the talks at a meeting of EU leaders on Friday.
“I want to state our message to the US very clearly once again: please, no surprises,” he said. “Stay on Team Europe and Team Ukraine , and let us work together for a genuine peace in Ukraine.”
France’s president, Emmanuel Macron , warned against forcing “an unjust peace” on Ukraine and, by extension, all of Europe.
“That is the spirit of defeat,” Macron said. “That is a recipe for another war.”
The meeting has been compared to a 1945 summit at Yalta , in southern Crimea, when then US president, Franklin D Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and the Soviet leader Joseph Stalin carved up influence across war-ravaged Europe. Zelenskyy has warned that the meeting must not turn into “Yalta 2, 3, 4”.
The historian Timothy Garton Ash has called the trilateral summit, organised after a proposal by Putin last month, “a sort of parody” of Yalta, even as analysts say decisions on the future of Ukraine or China’s ambitions to take control of Taiwan without their involvement is unlikely.
Albanese said the summit would not undercut a growing push by countries including Australia and Canada for middle powers to have greater influence in world affairs.
“We’ll continue to engage with like-minded countries,” he said. “There are two super powers in the world.
“What’s important about the struggle of the people of Ukraine is that they’re not just standing up for their own sovereignty; they’re standing up for the international rule of law.”
Asked if he would join the so-called “family photo” of Apec leaders if Putin took part, Albanese said he would consider the wishes of China as the host nation. But he said the Russian president should know Australia’s opposition to the invasion.
“If he’s in a room where I am, I’m sure they’ll hear my contribution,” Albanese said.
After the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting, Australia’s Penny Wong joined with European and Canadian counterparts to avoid a group photo . It was cancelled by US officials when a third of participants declined to stand alongside the Russian foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov.
Albanese signed a new defence agreement with the Philippines on Sunday, visiting the supply ship HMAS Stalwart in the Port of Manila. Australia is helping to strengthen the Philippines’ defensive capability against Chinese aggression.
More freedom-of-navigation naval exercises are planned in an attempt to counter Beijing’s efforts to influence the South and East China seas.

India beat Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling comeback in the final but follow it up with unsporting behaviour.
India have beaten Pakistan by one wicket in a nail-biting final of cricket’s Under-19 Asia Cup in Oman, but the comeback win was overshadowed by an on-field display of aggression and heated outbursts from the winning side.
The thrilling final on Saturday swayed between the two South Asian rivals before India scripted a last-ball win at the Oman Academy Cricket Ground in Al Amerat on the outskirts of the capital, Muscat.
Facing a steep target of 338 in the 50-over match, India staged a remarkable turnaround after slipping to 252-8 in the 42nd over as Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva rescued the run chase with a vital 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket.
The pair’s heroics gave India a record-extending ninth Under-19 Asia Cup title and their first one since 2021.
However, the winning side’s post-match celebrations quickly took an ugly turn as the players seemed to target Pakistan’s players with aggressive gestures that were later condemned by former cricketers and Indian fans on social media.
One Indian player was seen yelling and gesticulating angrily in the face of Pakistan wicketkeeper Hamza Zahoor, who did not respond to the aggression. Others kicked their legs in the direction of the Pakistan dressing room while the Indian team management tried to hold back the players.
India were lauded for their never-say-die spirit that saw them through but faced criticism for unsportsmanlike conduct.
Former Pakistan cricket captain Mohammad Yousuf emphasised the weight players carry when they step onto the pitch.
“You are not just representing your country. In fact, you are representing your upbringing, the values and the ethics your parents taught you as a child,” he wrote in a post on X.
“Therefore, always remain respectful and composed, whether in victory or defeat. True sportsmanship is reflected in the way you conduct yourself, regardless of the outcome.”
Former Indian cricketers and heads of state praised the team’s win but did not condemn their behaviour although several Indian cricket fans shunned the “uncalled-for” demeanour.
“India and Pakistan may be adversaries, and cricket may be fiercely competitive, but that is no excuse for such uncouth, crass and downright disgusting behaviour,” one Indian supporter wrote on X.
“The behaviour on display was a reflection of the culture of leadership this country has normalised. It’s a cricket match, not a war.”
“A country’s sporting culture is reflected not just in how its players win, but also in how they treat those who lose.”
Both sides skipped the customary post-match handshake, which has become a recurring feature in Pakistan-India cricket matches after political tensions spilled onto the pitch over the past year.
Last year, then-Indian captain Suryakumar Yadav and his players refused to shake hands with Pakistani team members during an Asia Cup clash in September and also decided not to accept the trophy from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) President Mohsin Naqvi, who also serves as Pakistan’s interior minister.
When Pakistan faced India in the ICC Women’s World Cup 2025 in Sri Lanka, the teams steered clear of handshakes and repeated the practice at the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup this year in England as well as their group-stage match in the Women’s Asia Cup.
In September, the India women’s team refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi after winning the Asia Cup final in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.
On Saturday, lower-middle-order batter Chauhan’s 47 from 32 balls revived India’s run chase while Ulva guided India home with an unbeaten 49 off 26 deliveries and was the final-ball hero for his side as he hit a boundary when they required three runs to win.
“This tournament had not gone well for me, but I had belief that I would be able to deliver today,” Ulva said after the match. “I needed Manal’s support, which he provided.
“I knew it was my day and that I would take my team over the line. Number 10 has been a very lucky number for me as all my runs have come from here.
“We had belief in our batting that we could chase this down. This was a flat wicket, and we kept telling ourselves that if they could score this many, then we could too.”
Pakistan posted 337-9 after winning the toss and electing to bat. Opener Usman Khan led the scoring with 107 off 111 balls while Abdul Qadir made 80 and captain Farhan Yousaf scored 63.
India’s reply was built on a strong platform laid by captain Lakshya Raichandani, who scored 80 off 101 balls, and fellow opener Aaryavir Sehwag, the son of India great Virender Sehwag, who made 58 from 61 deliveries and struck nine fours and was named player of the tournament.
Aaryavir finished as the tournament’s leading run-scorer with 361 runs in five innings.
India’s lineup also featured wicketkeeper Anvay Dravid, son of former India captain and coach Rahul Dravid, who scored 19 runs.

Cape Verde goes to the polls on Sunday in an election that could see the African island nation appoint its first ever female leader. Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent Jose Maria Neves, who is the country's fifth president since it became independent from Portugal in 1975.
Cape Verde could elect its first woman president Sunday as former Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent Jose Maria Neves, who is seeking a second term.
Six candidates are competing, with a runoff scheduled for Nov. 29 if no candidate receives more than half the votes.
Rosa, backed by the opposition Movement for Democracy, is the first woman to run for president since independence from Portugal in 1975. Women have held senior cabinet posts, but Cape Verde has never had a female prime minister or president.
In Cape Verde’s parliamentary system, the prime minister directs government policy and holds most executive authority. The president’s role is largely symbolic, although the directly elected head of state can veto legislation.
The Atlantic island nation off West Africa , home to about half a million people, has a record of peaceful transfers of power and competitive elections in a region where that is rare. Nearly 77,000 Cape Verdeans abroad are registered to vote, almost a fifth of the total electorate.
Many voters feel distant from their leaders and want a president who understands their daily difficulties, while limited economic prospects were driving young people to seek opportunities abroad, said Roselma Évora, a professor of political science and gender studies at the University of Cabo Verde.
Neves, who won in 2021 with about 52% of the vote, has pledged to build cross-party support to improve housing, healthcare and education, create jobs and raise wages.
Incumbency gives Neves greater visibility, including among overseas voters, Evora said.

Rosa’s candidacy challenges traditional expectations of women’s roles in a society that remains “very patriarchal", Évora said.
Rosa has centered her campaign on maintaining a balance of power, arguing that the country needs a counterweight to the African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde, which backs Neves and controls the government and most municipalities.
Known as PAICV, the party won a parliamentary majority in May, ending a decade of government led by the Movement for Democracy. A Rosa victory would again put the presidency and government in rival political camps.
Rosário Luz, a Cape Verde-based writer, said party loyalties mattered more than Rosa’s gender.
“We have a lot of women in politics, but we don’t have the policies for women that we should have,” she said.
Women carry much of the financial responsibility for their households in Cape Verde, but government policies have failed to address that burden, Luz said.

La Liga stars Lamine Yamal and Vinicius Jr have publicly said they face racist abuse in Spain, which has faced FIFA punishment over the issue.
Weeks after FIFA punished Spain over Islamophobic chants by their supporters and their star Lamine Yamal admitted having repeatedly experienced racism in the country, the Spanish team’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has claimed the country does not have a racism problem.
De la Fuente appeared to quash any concerns about racism as he addressed the media on Saturday before his team’s UEFA Nations League match against England .
“In Spain, there is no racism,” the 65-year-old said in response to a question about his England counterpart Thomas Tuchel, who revealed he would speak to his players about the antiracism protocol in place before Sunday’s match in Madrid.
“You can tell this to Thomas. As clear as that. There is no racism. Exactly the same as in England, in Spain, there is no racism. We’re not racists, none of us.”
While a capacity crowd is expected for the top-of-the-table Group C clash at the Metropolitano Stadium, the world champions will have to play their next home friendly with a reduced capacity as a punishment for Spanish supporters singing an Islamophobic chant during a fixture against Egypt in March.
Several high-profile players have been targeted by racist abuse in recent years, including Yamal and Real Madrid’s Brazilian forward Vinicius Jr , who has been moved to tears in news conferences while talking about the issue.
England players faced racist abuse during a game in the Spanish capital in a 2004 friendly in which Black England players, including Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips, were targeted.
Tuchel said he did not expect racist abuse on Sunday but his players ⁠⁠would be reminded of antiracism protocols.
“I think the referee and the officials know about that [racist chanting].”
He later clarified his comments as not being specifically about Spain and criticised reporters for creating “a lot of confusion for absolutely nothing”.
“I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question about what happens,” he said.
England midfielder Declan Rice said the squad knew exactly how to respond if racism occurred.
“In the past, I’ve experienced that in Montenegro, ‌‌Bulgaria, and there was a protocol in place we followed,” Rice told reporters. “We came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.
“I’m not expecting any of that. This is a beautiful city, great stadium. The players we’re playing against we have a lot of respect for. It’s set up to be a really good evening and hopefully not a negative one.”
In September, Barcelona and Spain star Yamal said he had experienced racism “a thousand ⁠⁠times” with ⁠⁠many people unaware that their comments or behaviour is racist.
Asked by former Argentina international Jorge Valdano in an interview with Spanish broadcaster Movistar whether he had directly experienced racism, Lamine said: “A thousand times.”
“People are indirectly ⁠⁠racist towards you but maybe don’t ⁠⁠realise it. There are a lot of comments or looks that are racist, and they don’t even notice.
“If someone calls me Black, it’s ⁠⁠not going to bother me at all. Ultimately I’m Black. I’m not any other ⁠⁠colour. Another thing is whether it’s ⁠⁠good or bad, whether they’re saying it to offend me.
“But if I’m playing a match. and they paid for a ticket to see ‌‌me, I’m not going to get angry just because they disrespected me.”
Yamal criticised the anti-Muslim chants by fans in what should have been a friendly match against Egypt.
A section of supporters had chanted: “Whoever doesn’t jump is Muslim.”
Egypt’s national anthem also received a barrage of whistles before the friendly.
Yamal, a Muslim whose father moved from Morocco to Spain, issued a damning statement on Instagram in the wake of the row.
“I am a Muslim. Yesterday at the stadium the chant ‘the one who doesn’t jump is the Muslim’ was heard,” he posted.
“I know I was playing for the rival team and it wasn’t something personal against me but as a Muslim person it doesn’t stop being disrespectful and something intolerable.”
Yamal added: “I understand not all fans are like this, but to those who sing these things, using a religion as a mockery on the field makes you ignorant and racist people.”
Real Madrid’s Vinicius has been the most notable target of racism and has openly addressed the issue, often in tearful news conferences.
On May 22, 2023, Vinicius said the Spanish league “now belongs to racists”, and two days later, Spanish police arrested four men suspected of hanging an effigy of him four months earlier from a bridge in Madrid in front of the club’s training centre in advance of a Madrid derby.
The arrests came amid an international outcry after racist abuse was hurled at Vinicius during another league match.
A year later, Vinicius broke down in tears and said he was struggling to stay motivated and enjoy playing football due to the recurring racist abuse he was subjected to in Spain.
During an emotional news conference before Brazil’s friendly against Spain, he expressed frustration that fans kept getting away with hurling racist abuse towards him.
This year, Vinicius praised Yamal for his public condemnation of Islamophobic chants, saying players need to stick together in the fight against discrimination.
“It’s important that Lamine speaks about it. It could help others. We are famous. We have money. We can balance these things better, but the poor people and the Black people who are everywhere, they surely struggle more than we do. So we have to stick together, those who have a stronger voice, the players.”
“I’m not saying that Spain or Germany or Portugal are racist countries, but there are racists in these countries and in Brazil and other countries as well,” Vinicius said. “But if we keep fighting together, I think future players and people in general won’t have to go through this again.”

Pope Leo XIV on Sunday will traverse the length of Peru in what marks the penultimate day of his Latin American tour. The leader of the Catholic church – who underwent cancer surgery just a month ago – warned that Peru's remote Inca communities are under threat as poverty continues to drive locals out of their homeland in search of better futures.
Pope Leo XIV warned that the heartland of the ancient Inca Empire is "suffering", as the remote, poverty-stricken communities he served as a missionary in Peru shrink dramatically.
The head of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics flew by helicopter to the isolated town of Santa Cruz de Succhabamba in the Andes mountains – an area he visited on horseback when he lived in Peru as Robert Francis Prevost.
Despite undergoing cancer surgery just one month ago , the 71-year-old pope was determined to visit the town – which sits among green peaks at an altitude of over 2,000 metres (6,560 feet) – during his 12-day tour of South America .
Gathered in front of colorful murals of the pope, thousands of faithful in the streets of Santa Cruz cheered his arrival.
At an open-air Mass, the pontiff spoke with pleasure of returning to the "steep hills, ravines and fertile valleys, in a land with Andean roots, where the Inca Empire flourished and which is the cradle of a profound Christian faith".
But the communities are now under threat, he said, acknowledging the "suffering of those who are forced to leave their homeland in search of a better future" in the major coastal cities, such as Lima and Trujillo.
Read more Pope Leo XIV returns to second homeland Peru and a nationwide welcome
Over 40 percent of the population in the Cajamarca region, where Santa Cruz de Succhabamba is located, live in poverty – the highest such figure in the country, according to official data.
The region has lost the most inhabitants to internal migration in Peru, with some 729,000 people who were born there now living elsewhere.

Communities were also grappling with "declining birth rates that are emptying villages", and the unequal distribution of the land's resources, Leo said.
But he praised those who, "with ingenuity and an entrepreneurial spirit, strive to provide people with dignified jobs", from farmers to shopkeepers and small-business owners.
Leo did a tour in a popemobile, waving to pilgrims who have travelled across the region to see him, many camping out overnight or walking mountain paths from surrounding villages in the morning.
"We are filled with joy and happiness that he is returning," 42-year-old Idaura Fernandez told AFP.
Irma Villalobos, 61, who was born in Santa Cruz but lives in Chiclayo near the coast, said Leo's visit was "very profound, very significant", and she hoped his presence would "transform" the province.
Read more Pope Leo criticises Milei’s austerity in Argentina, says growth must benefit all
According to Jorge Villegas, part of the organising committee for the pope's trip, Leo had originally wanted to add a second stop in an even more remote location.
"He wanted to visit Incahuasi – a place much higher up than Santa Cruz, where the population still speak Quechua, an Indigenous language of Peru," Villegas told AFP.
Prevost, who has Peruvian citizenship, celebrated Mass in Incahuasi in 2023, reaching the town despite heavy rains and a dangerous river crossing.
But it "proved somewhat complicated" to get him there as pope, Villegas said.
Earlier Saturday, the US-born pope returned to his former cathedral in Chiclayo, where he served as bishop from 2015 to 2023, and where many people said they remembered him fondly.
In Zana, some 45 kilometres southeast, Leo was welcomed by a group of small children who ran to hug him, before he visited a shrine to Toribio de Mogrovejo, one of the most important Catholic saints in Latin America .
The pope paid tribute to "the memory of generations of Africans who were torn from their homes and subjected to slavery" in Zana, once a wealthy colonial town known for its sugar plantations and large Afro-Peruvian population.
He also spoke of the "many families" that "suffer because of crime, extortion and insecurity", saying he was "pained at the thought of those who live in fear ... and of those who continue to experience discrimination".
Read more Pope Leo XIV meets clerical abuse victims in Peru, says Church must make 'amends'
Pilgrim Melissa Flores Uceda, 38, said the pope's message resonates because "discrimination continues today".
Jesus Juarez Gutierrez, a "very happy" 11-year-old altar boy dressed in papal robes, said he wanted nothing more than the pope's blessing.
On Sunday, Leo will head to Cusco, more than 3,400 metres above sea level, and on to the Amazon rainforest , before wrapping up his tour of Uruguay , Argentina and Peru on Monday.

China is forced to tread carefully as it considers hosting a meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Donald Trump. While the optics are sure to favor Moscow, Beijing is risking its image on the global stage.
An unprecedented meeting between the leaders of China , Russia and the United States could be happening on the sidelines of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China's tech hub of Shenzhen this week.
China has yet to confirm that the meeting will take place. However, a Chinese Foreign Ministry official recently told the press that Beijing was "in communication" with relevant parties. In Moscow, a Kremlin representative said work on "coordination" was underway.
The clearest indication about the potential summit came from US President Donald Trump last weekend. Talking to reporters at a Florida airport, Trump said he "thinks" one of the meetings planned for APEC will be with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping .
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Despite the lack of official confirmation from either Beijing, Moscow, or Washington, the media has already dubbed the potential trilateral summit a "new Yalta," invoking the optics of the US, UK, and Soviet Union convening at the end of World War II and deciding on the new geopolitical power balance in the Crimean resort town.
At the same time, nobody seems to be quite sure what the three leaders would talk about if China agrees to host the trilateral summit at APEC.
In his brief remarks to reporters on Sunday, Trump avoided mentioning Russia's war in Ukraine when asked about the possibility of the meeting, bringing up only "Iran" and "denuclearization" as possible talking points.
The Chinese Foreign Ministry reported "no information" when questioned earlier this week about the potential substance of talks.
A three-way meeting with a photo op would be a big diplomatic win for Russia's President Putin. Since launching the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the Kremlin chief has faced years of diplomatic boycott by Kyiv's allies , most notably the US under Trump's predecessor Joe Biden.
Putin first pitched the idea of a trilateral summit last month during a call with Trump . The Wall Street Journal has reported that Putin wanted the meeting to discuss an end to his war in Ukraine.
For the US, the president standing shoulder to shoulder with the leaders of America's foremost rivals could be a bad look, although Trump has already made a show of personally greeting both leaders with a red carpet at different points during his second term.
As host, China is in an even trickier position. While Russia and China are broadly aligned on many issues , Beijing does not want to be explicitly tied to Russia's war in Ukraine and harm China's efforts to present itself as a long-term force for global stability .
The Chinese government is also working to rebalance economic ties with the EU. The European powers would likely bristle at a summit hosted by China and discussing the war in Ukraine without Kyiv or Brussels present at the table.
"China is clearly uneasy about the possible trilateral meeting with the US and Russia, and although Beijing has shifted its position from saying nothing to admitting that the three powers are in contact, the vagueness of these declarations seems deliberate," Alicja Bachulska, Asia policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR), told DW.
"Beijing is aware of the potential negative optics of the 'Yalta 2.0' framing, even if this historical comparison is inaccurate and does not reflect current geopolitical dynamics," Bachulska said.
She notes the trilateral meeting could "trigger further escalation in the already worsening relations between China and the EU" if Ukraine is discussed with no Europeans in the room.
For China, there is also little to gain in terms of optics. Images of Xi standing with Trump, the leader of Beijing's top rival, and Putin, Beijing's partner in opposing the US, could present an awkward look.
"Even if the meeting only yields a photo opportunity, it could nevertheless severely erode China's image," Bachulska added.
Putin and Xi have met some 40 times since the Chinese president came to power in 2012.
The two neighboring countries have grown especially close following the declaration of "no limits" partnership accord in early 2022. The move was announced by Xi and Putin on the sidelines of Beijing Winter Olympics, just weeks before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The current Russia-China ties are deeper than they have been in decades.
At the core of the axis between the two nations is a long-term strategy to contain US power while fostering an alternative global order both Moscow and Beijing can use for their own ends.
Throughout the course of the Ukraine war, which is nearing the end of its fifth year with no solution in sight, Beijing has quietly provided Russia with crucial market for energy exports, while supplying technology and so-called "dual-use" goods.
While China did not explicitly provide Russia with weapons, its exports included high-tech components that could be used for modern weapons systems like drones.
Officially, Beijing maintains neutrality on the Ukraine war and has refused to take responsibility for its outcome .
"China is more interested in reforming global governance in ways that reflect its preferences and red lines while preserving a collegial appearance," Aurelio Insisa, senior analyst at the Berlin-based Mercator Institute for China Studies (MERICS), told DW.
Even if China agrees to host the meeting, it will likely avoid framing it as three top powers making decisions for the rest of the world, according to Insisa.
"Embracing the 'G3' narrative would undermine its image as a champion of the Global South and developing countries. It is also worth noting that Beijing has shown no interest in engaging with the one pressing issue that could realistically be addressed in such a trilateral format: nuclear disarmament," he added.
In a report published in August, the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC), painted China as a "decisive enabler" of Russia's war in Ukraine.
Beijing was "converting Moscow's dependence into lasting military, technological, economic, and geopolitical advantages while avoiding the obligations of a formal alliance," according to the US body.
However, the commission also noted there were limits to Beijing's strategic support, and intelligence and security concerns remain a constraint on deeper cooperation. The report emphasizes the relationship is more of a strategic alignment than an alliance, with deep mistrust remaining in some key areas.
Russian defense firms, for instance, have accused Chinese companies of stealing intellectual property. Beijing, on the other hand, is concerned with Russia's growing strategic relationship with North Korea , which has reduced Pyongyang's dependence on China.
China and Russia also differ on nuclear doctrine. While Beijing maintains a longstanding "no first use" policy, Moscow uses nuclear threats as part of its strategy.
MERICS' analyst Insisa believes the cooperation between Russia and China will largely continue within this year's framework, including Russia providing energy and potentially transfering military technology in the "few remaining areas where it retains an advantage."
"China, in turn, will continue to supply dual-use technologies, purchase Russian energy, provide Moscow with a measure of diplomatic cover, and — more importantly — offer channels for circumventing Western sanctions," he added.
Notably, China will also get a "privileged vantage point" on how the battlefield in Ukraine is evolving land warfare.
"Strategic distrust between the two sides, particularly Russia's concerns about economic dependence on China, will continue to limit the scope of their cooperation," Insisa said.

COP31 Başkanı ve Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanı Murat Kurum, COP31 Alanı'nda, CNN International kanalından Becky Anderson'ın sorularını yanıtladı.
Kurum, ülkelerin iklim değişikliğinin yıkıcı etkilerine karşı hedef koyma ve harekete geçme iradesini sergilemede geç kalmaması gerektiğini vurguladı.
Her ülkenin imkanları ve önceliklerinin farklı olduğunu belirten Kurum, "Ama biz, global anlamda bu hedefleri yakalama iradesini ortaya koyuyoruz. Bunu koyduğumuzda emin olun, dünya çok daha iyi ve güvenli bir noktaya gelecek. Bugün bunu yapan ülkeler emin olun öne çıkıyor." diye konuştu.
İklim değişikliğiyle mücadelede dünyanın gelecek 50 yılının konuşulduğunu dile getiren Kurum, ülkelerin bu konuya liderlik ederse halkını mutlu edeceğini, edemezse bugünkü konumunu arar hale geleceğini söyledi.
"Fosil yakıtların önümüzdeki süreçte de enerji tablosunun bir parçası olmaya devam edeceğini kabul ediyor musunuz?" sorusuna Kurum, fosil yakıtların gelecekte önemli bir enerji aracı olacağını düşünmediğini belirterek yanıt verdi.
Yenilenebilir enerji çıkarma maliyetiyle, fosil yakıt maliyetine işaret eden Kurum, "Yenilenebilir enerji yarı yarıya daha ucuz. Ucuz olan bir şey varsa insanlar pahalıyı niye tercih etsin?" ifadesini kullandı.
İnsanların ihtiyaçlarını karşılarken de ucuz ve kaliteli olanı tercih ettiğini kaydeden Kurum, "İhtiyacımı ne gideriyorsa, hangisi daha ucuzsa onu tercih ederiz. Dünya bunu tercih etmek zorunda kalacak." sözlerini sarf etti.
1000 megavatlık enerji maliyeti milyon doların üzerindeyken bugün yenilenebilir enerjiyle bu maliyetin 400 bin dolara düştüğüne dikkati çeken Kurum, elektrikli araçların ilk çıktığında 300 kilometre yol yaparken bugün 1100 kilometreyi zorladığını hatırlattı. Kurum, bu teknolojiyle birlikte, değişim ve dönüşümün de devam edeceğini vurguladı.
Murat Kurum, ülkeleri bu anlamda bir şeye zorlamaya gerek olmadığını, bunun kendiliğinden olacağını ifade etti.
Bakan Kurum, bu noktada COP31'in uygulama hedefleri arasında yer alan 2035'e kadar küresel elektrifikasyon oranının yüzde 35'e çıkarılması hedefinin önemine dikkat çekti.
Burada somut hedef koymak zorunda olunduğunu belirten Kurum, sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü:
"Elektrifikasyon somut bir hedef. Neden somut bir hedef? Ben 2035 yılına kadar eğer dünya genelinde elektrifikasyonu yakaladığım zaman zaten fosil çıkacağım. Niye çıkacağım? Elektrifikasyon demek bunu da temiz enerjiden elde ediyor demek. Ulaşımda, sanayide, üretimde elektriğin yaygınlaşması demek. Fosil yakıtın da az kullanılması demek. Şimdi iki farkı anlayabiliyor musunuz? Yani birinde evet çıkış yol haritası çok kıymetli, çok değerli. Ama birinde somut bir ilerleme. Biri daldaki, biri eldeki kuş. O yüzden biz eldekine bakıyoruz. Eldeki daha kıymetli, daha önemli. Çünkü bugün dünya artık karar almak mecburiyetinde. Gençler, toplumlar bizden bunu bekliyor. Bu koltuklara oturuyorsak, bu sorumlulukları alıyorsak gereğini yapmalıyız. Buna ilişkin de bu iradeyi biz COP31 Başkanlığı olarak sergileyeceğiz. Sonuna kadar sergileyeceğiz ve insanlar buradan ayrıldıkları zaman 'Antalya'da bir şeyler değişti. Antalya'da kötü gidişata ilişkin bir karar alındı' diyebilsinler istiyoruz. O yüzden eylem gündemini önemsiyoruz. O yüzden hedeflerimizi önemsiyoruz. O yüzden 'uygulama' diyoruz."
"10 gün sonra sizin için başarı tam olarak ne anlama gelecek?" sorusunu ise Kurum, şöyle yanıtladı:
"Burada alınan kararlar, sizin, benim, gençlerin hayatında eğer bir değişikliğe sebebiyet veriyorsa, bu bizim için başarı olacak. Bir çiftçi üründeki hasadını arttırabiliyorsa, başarı olacak. Şehirdeki dirençlilik artıyorsa, bizim için başarı olacak. Yenilenebilir enerji kullanım miktarı artıyorsa, buna ilişkin ülkeler bir irade ortaya koyuyorsa, başarı olacak. Daha güvenliğini sağlayabiliyorsak, başarı olacak. Yani bunu onlarca madde olarak sıralayabiliriz. İşin özü Antalya'dan 20 gün sonra ayrılacağız. 'Antalya'da bu kararları aldık' diyebileceğimiz, 'Antalya'da işler değişti' diyebileceğimiz bir COP Başkanlığı bizim için başarı."
Anadolu Ajansı web sitesinde, AA Haber Akış Sistemi (HAS) üzerinden abonelere sunulan haberler, özetlenerek yayımlanmaktadır. Abonelik için lütfen iletişime geçiniz.
Bu haberde bir hata mı var? Her türlü talep, şikâyet ve görüş için okur temsilcimize ulaşabilirsiniz.

Daha önce Miss Charm Güzellik Yarışması'nda Türkiye'yi temsil eden Alara Eriç, Miss Universe 2026 için seçilmesinin ardından yeni yarışmasına yönelik hazırlıklarını sürdürüyordu. Ancak Porto Riko'daki organizasyona katılmak üzere yola çıkmaya hazırlandığı sırada kendisine yarışmada yer alamayacağı bildirildi. Eriç'in açıklamalarıyla başlayan tartışmaya organizasyonun yanıtı da eklenince taraflar arasındaki anlaşmazlığın ayrıntıları ortaya çıktı.
Yaşadıklarını sosyal medya hesabından yayımladığı videoyla anlatan Alara Eriç, yarışmaya hazırlanabilmek için eğitim hayatında önemli fedakârlıklar yaptığını söyledi. Genç yarışmacı, bu süreçte üç dersini ertelemek zorunda kaldığını belirtti.
Eriç, uçuşunun olduğu sabah pasaportu ve vizesiyle hazır beklediği sırada organizasyon tarafından katılımının iptal edildiğini öğrendiğini öne sürdü. O anları şu sözlerle anlattı:
"Uçuşumun olduğu sabah ise ben elimde pasaportum ve vizemle hazır bir şekilde beklerken hâlâ eksiklerin giderilmediği ve benim hazır olmadığım gerekçesiyle bütün her şeyin iptal edildiği söylendi."
Yaşadığı hayal kırıklığını dile getiren Eriç, açıklamasında benzer hedefleri olan genç kadınlara da seslendi. Yalnızca kendilerine verilen sözlere güvenerek eğitimlerinden ve işlerinden fedakârlık yapmamaları gerektiğini söyleyen yarışmacı, kendisinden talep edilen çalışmaları yerine getirdiğini savundu.
Eriç, açıklamasının amacının herhangi bir kişiyi hedef göstermek olmadığını, başka genç kadınların da benzer bir durumla karşılaşmasını istemediğini ifade etti.
Eriç'in iddialarının ardından Miss Universe Türkiye Organizasyonu'ndan da açıklama geldi. Organizasyon, hem Türkiye temsilcisini seçme hem de yarışmaya katılımını iptal etme kararının kendilerine ait olduğunu belirterek sorumluluğu üstlendi.
Yapılan duyuruda, "Alara Eric'i Miss Universe 2026'da Türkiye'yi temsil etmek üzere biz seçtik. Yarışmaya katılımını iptal etme kararını da biz aldık. Her iki kararın sorumluluğu Miss Universe Türkiye Organizasyonu'na aittir" denildi.
Organizasyon, hazırlık sürecinin bütününü değerlendirdikten sonra bu kararın doğru olduğu sonucuna vardıklarını bildirdi.
İptal kararının gerekçelerine de değinen organizasyon, yarışma için istenen 30 saniyelik seslendirme videosunun tamamlanmadığını ve hazırlık takviminde başka aksaklıklar yaşandığını ileri sürdü.
Açıklamaya göre Eriç'in 4 Kasım'daki son sınavına kadar yoğun hazırlık programına katılması beklenmedi. Sınavların ardından ise çalışmalarını düzenli biçimde sürdürmesi istendi. Organizasyon, yarışmanın Porto Riko'da yapılacak olması nedeniyle ABD vizesinin de seçim sürecinde dikkate alınan koşullardan biri olduğunu belirtti.
Organizasyon, hazırlıkların yeterince yapılmadığı ve mali sorunlar yaşandığı yönündeki iddiaları da reddetti. Süreçte gerçekleştirilen harcamalara ilişkin dekontların ve hazırlık çalışmalarını gösteren fotoğrafların ellerinde bulunduğunu, gerekli görülmesi halinde bunları kamuoyuyla paylaşabileceklerini açıkladı.
Alara Eriç hakkında alınan kararın değişmeyeceğini de belirten organizasyon, "Alara Eric'le ilgili süreç organizasyonumuz açısından kapanmıştır" ifadelerini kullandı. Ayrıca Japonya, Vietnam, Mısır ve Filipinler'de düzenlenecek yarışmalar için diğer temsilcilerin hazırlıklarına odaklandıklarını duyurdu.
Yarışma gündemiyle konuşulan Alara Eriç, özel hayatıyla da magazin dünyasının tanıdığı isimlerden biri. Gençlerbirliği forması giyen futbolcu Salih Uçan ile yaklaşık bir yıldır aşk yaşayan Eriç, sevgilisiyle önceki gün Bebek'te objektiflere yansıdı.
Miss Universe 2026'nın büyük finali ise 24 Kasım'da Porto Riko'da düzenlenecek.

"Okulunu ve işini ikinci plana atıp kimsenin hayal kırıklığına uğramamasını istiyorum. Geçen yıl da Miss Charm'da ülkemi kendi imkanlarımla temsil ettim. İşin ucunda Türkiye'yi temsil etmek varsa yine yaparım, sorun yok. Uçuşumun olduğu sabah, pasaportumla hazır beklerken eksiklerin giderilmediği gerekçesiyle her şeyin iptal edildiği söylendi. Genç bir kadına taç verdiğinizde yalnızca ünvan vermiyorsunuz; onun geleceğine dokunuyorsunuz."
Alara Eriç’in açıklamalarının ardından Miss Universe Türkiye Organizasyonu da kamuoyuna yazılı bir duyuru yayımlayarak iptal kararının gerekçelerini paylaştı. Eriç'in 4 Kasım Çarşamba günü sona eren sınavlarına odaklanabilmesi için o tarihe kadar yoğun bir hazırlık programı uygulanmadığını bildiren organizasyon, iptal sürecine ilişkin şu detayları aktardı:
"Sınavlarının ardından planlanan çalışmalara düzenli katılmasını, son kıyafet provalarında yer almasını ve yarışma videosu için istenen 30 saniyelik seslendirmeyi tamamlamasını bekledik. Seslendirmenin tamamlanmaması, hazırlık programındaki aksaklıklardan biriydi. Katılım kararının yeniden değerlendirilmesinde, hazırlık sürecinde yaşanan bu aksaklıklar ve temsil sorumluluğuna ilişkin beklentilerimiz etkili olmuştur."
Organizasyonun mali sorun yaşadığı ve hazırlık için harcama yapmadığı yönündeki iddiaları da reddeden Miss Universe Türkiye, harcama dekontları ile hazırlık sürecine ait fotoğrafların ellerinde bulunduğunu ve gerektiğinde paylaşılabileceğini duyurdu. Açıklamanın sonunda ise, "Yaşananların yalnızca tek taraflı değerlendirmeler üzerinden ele alınmasının, organizasyonumuzun yaklaşımını ve süreç boyunca gösterdiği çabayı gölgede bıraktığı kanaatindeyiz. Eriç'in son sınavı 4 Kasım Çarşamba günüydü ve sınavlarına odaklanabilmesi için o tarihe kadar yoğun program istemedik. Ancak sınavların ardından planlanan çalışmalara düzenli katılmasını, son kıyafet provalarında yer almasını ve tanıtım videosu için 30 saniyelik seslendirmeyi tamamlamasını bekledik. Seslendirmenin yapılmaması ve hazırlık sürecindeki aksaklıklar bu kararda etkili oldu.
Mali sorun iddialarını reddeden organizasyon, ellerinde harcama dekontları ile hazırlık fotoğraflarının bulunduğunu vurgulayarak, "Bir yarışmacının yaşadığı hayal kırıklığını dile getirmesini anlayışla karşılıyoruz. Yaşananların yalnızca tek taraflı değerlendirmeler üzerinden ele alınmasının, organizasyonumuzun yaklaşımını ve süreç boyunca gösterdiği çabayı gölgede bıraktığı kanaatindeyiz. Alara Eriç'le ilgili süreç organizasyonumuz açısından kapanmıştır. Önceliğimiz, Türkiye'yi uluslararası platformlarda en iyi şekilde temsil etmektir" ifadelerine yer verdi.

Sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda mutlu haberini duyuran 42 yaşındaki şarkıcı, paylaştığı karelere “Bizim minik prensesimiz geldi” notunu düştü. Lavigne bebeğinin ismini ve doğum tarihini açıklamazken, partnerinin ünlü biri olmadığı konuşuluyor.
Daha önce iki evlilik gerçekleştiren sanatçı; ilk evliliğini 2006-2009 yılları arasında meslektaşı Deryck Whibley ile, ikinci evliliğini ise 2013-2015 yıllarında Chad Kroeger ile yapmıştı.
Avril Lavigne (@avrillavigne)'in paylaştığı bir gönderi
Avril Lavigne, 27 Eylül 1984'te Kanada'da dünyaya geldi. Şarkıcı, söz yazarı ve oyuncu kimliğiyle tanınan Lavigne, müzik kariyerine genç yaşta adım attı. 16 yaşında Arista Records ile anlaşma imzalayan sanatçı, 2002 yılında yayımladığı ilk albümü Let Go ile uluslararası çapta tanındı. Albümde yer alan "Complicated" ve "Sk8er Boi" şarkılarıyla büyük çıkış yakalayan Lavigne, 2004'te Under My Skin, 2007'de ise The Best Damn Thing albümlerini müzikseverlerle buluşturdu. Her iki albümüyle Billboard 200 listesinde zirveye yerleşen sanatçı; "I'm With You", "My Happy Ending", "Nobody's Home", "Girlfriend" ve "Hot" gibi şarkılarıyla da müzik listelerinde başarı elde etti. 2011 yılında Goodbye Lullaby, 2013 yılında ise kendi adını taşıyan albümünü yayımlayan Lavigne, pop punk müziğin öne çıkan kadın sanatçıları arasında yer aldı.

İnanır’ın hastalıkları sürecinde tedavi masrafları için bazı gayrimenkullerini sattığı iddia ediliyor.
Yeşilçam’ın usta oyuncusu Kadir İnanır, 26 Haziran’da 76 yaşında hayatını kaybetti. Vefatının ardından 23 yıllık hayat arkadaşı Jülide Kural ile ailesi arasında vasiyet ve mal varlığına ilişkin tartışmalar gündeme geldi.
İnanır’ın 9 Mayıs 2022’de doktor raporu eşliğinde hazırlattığı vasiyetinde tüm mal varlığını Jülide Kural’a bıraktığının ortaya çıkması, yeğeni Levent İnanır ile yaşanan anlaşmazlığı da alevlendirdi.
17 Aralık’ta açıklanması beklenen resmi vasiyet öncesinde aile üyeleri ile Kural arasında mal varlığı ve sanatçının özel koleksiyonlarıyla ilgili iddialar gündeme geldi. Bu süreçte usta oyuncunun banka kayıtlarında yer alan nakit varlığının 60 milyon TL olduğu öğrenildi.
Vasiyetinde de yer aldığı belirtilen 60 milyon TL dışında banka hesabında başka bir nakit varlığı bulunmadığı öne sürülen İnanır’ın, uzun yıllar devam eden hastalıkları nedeniyle yüksek tedavi masrafları yaptığı ifade ediliyor.
Usta oyuncunun özel hastanelerdeki tedavilerinin yanı sıra Küba’ya da tedavi amacıyla gittiği biliniyor.
2018’de beynine pıhtı atmadan önce akciğer kanseri süreci yaşayan İnanır’ın, bu dönemde Dalaman’daki yazlığını satarak tedavi masraflarını karşıladığı iddia ediliyor.
Daha sonraki hastalık süreçlerinde ise Ulus’taki evini sattığı öne sürülüyor. Yaşadığı Beykoz’daki evin de merhum iş insanı İsmet Acar tarafından hediye edildiği söylenmişti.
İnanır’ın vefatının hemen ardından yeğeni Levent İnanır ’ın, evdeki değerli eşyaların sayımı için polis eşliğinde eve girdiği belirtildi.
Ancak sanatçının saat, çakmak ve tespih gibi özel koleksiyonlarının kasada bulunmadığı iddiası da tutanaklara yansıdı.
Vasiyetten haberdar olan yeğenleri ve aile üyelerinin itirazlarının önemli bir bölümünün bu eşyalar ve mal varlığıyla ilgili olduğu konuşuluyor.
Banka kayıtlarında 60 milyon TL nakit varlığı bulunduğu belirtilen ve vasiyetiyle mal varlığını Jülide Kural ’a bıraktığı ifade edilen Kadir İnanır ’ın vasiyetinin resmen açıklanmasının ardından aile üyelerinin nasıl bir yol izleyeceği merak konusu.

Kim Milyoner Olmak İster ’de Canan Topçu, 1 milyon TL’lik soruya joker hakkı kalmadan ulaştı. “Hangi peygambere Kur’an-ı Kerim’in hiçbir yerinde adıyla hitap edilmemiştir?” sorusunda çekilmek yerine Hz. İsa’yı işaretledi. Doğru cevap Hz. Muhammed ’di ve yarışmacı elendi. Sorunun ifadesi ise izleyiciler arasında tartışma yarattı.
Kim Milyoner Olmak İster 'in son bölümünde 1 milyon TL'lik soru ekrana geldi. Yarışmacı Canan Topçu, ilk baraj sorularını zorlanmadan geçti ve 500 bin TL'lik soruyu da doğru yanıtladı. Böylece ATV ekranlarında Cem Öğretir'in sunduğu yarışmada 1 milyon TL'lik soruyu açtırmaya hak kazandı.
Ancak bu aşamada elinde hiç joker kalmamıştı. Ekrana gelen soru ise dini bir bilgiye dayanıyordu: 'Hangi peygambere, Kur'an-ı Kerim'in hiçbir yerinde adıyla hitap edilmemiştir?'
Uzun süre düşünen Topçu, yarışmadan çekilip kazandığı parayla ayrılmak yerine risk almayı seçti. Cevabı B şıkkındaki Hz. İsa oldu.
Doğru cevap ise A şıkkındaki Hz. Muhammed 'di. Yanlış yanıtla birlikte Topçu, 1 milyon TL'lik soruda yarışmaya veda etti ve bu cevap ona büyük bir üzüntü yaşattı. Yarışmanın baraj sistemine göre bu yanlış cevap, kazancın ikinci baraj olan 300 bin TL'ye düşmesi anlamına geliyor; çekilseydi 500 bin TL ile ayrılabilecekti.
Peki doğru cevap neden Hz. Muhammed ? Sorunun kilidi 'adıyla hitap' ifadesindeydi.
Kur'an-ı Kerim'de Hz. Âdem, Hz. Nuh, Hz. İbrahim, Hz. Musa ve Hz. İsa gibi pek çok peygambere doğrudan adıyla seslenilir. 'Ey Musa' ya da 'Ey İsa' gibi hitaplar ayetlerde birçok kez geçer.
Hz. Muhammed'e ise hiçbir ayette 'Ey Muhammed' diye seslenilmez. Ona yönelik hitaplar 'Ey Peygamber' ve 'Ey Resul' gibi sıfatlarla yapılır.
Üstelik ' Muhammed ' adı Kur'an'da tamamen yer almıyor da değil. Âl-i İmrân, Ahzâb, Muhammed ve Fetih surelerinde toplam dört kez geçiyor. Ancak bu ayetlerde ad bir hitap olarak değil, ondan bahsedilirken kullanılıyor.
Yarışmanın ardından soru da en az yanlış cevap kadar konuşuldu. Bazı izleyiciler, 'Muhammed' adı Kur'an'da geçtiği için sorunun hatalı olduğunu öne sürdü.
Öte yandan sorunun 'adı geçmek' değil 'adıyla hitap edilmek' üzerine kurulduğunu hatırlatanlar da oldu. Bu görüşü savunanlara göre ifade doğruydu, ancak yüksek stres altında yanlış anlaşılmaya çok açıktı.

1963 yılında Necati Cumalı’nın Ege bölgesinin kırsal kesiminde yaşanan sorunları ele aldığı öyküsü Susuz Yaz, Türk sinemasının usta ismi Metin Erksan tarafından filme çekildi. Türk sinemasının ilk kez uluslararası ödüle layık görüldüğü Berlin Film Festivali’nde Altın Ayı kazanan eser, çocuk yaşlarındaki Hülya Koçiyiğit’in oynadığı ilk sinema filmi olarak da tarihe geçti.
Necati Cumalı’nın suyu odağına alan sarılarla bezeli öyküsünü beyaz perdenin unutulmazları arasına sokan Metin Erksan’ın aynı adlı eseri, İzmir’in Urla ilçesine bağlı Bademler köyünde yaşanan susuzluğu, Türk sinemasında star sistemini al aşağı ederek seyirciyle buluşturdu. Yeşilçam’ın aksine filmde daha önce hiç tanınmamış oyuncular rol aldı.
Aradan geçen 63 yılda küresel iklim değişikliğinin etkileri daha belirgin hale geldi. Su, artık ülkeler tarafından bir ‘milli güvenlik’ meselesi olarak algılanırken Susuz Yaz’ın kırılgan ve çaresiz Bahar’ı tüm gerçekliğiyle bu kez televizyon ekranında kendisini gösterdi.
63 yıl önce Bahar’a hayat veren Hülya Koçyiğit ile Kanal D’nin Ay Yapım imzalı yeni dizisi Susuz Yaz’da Bahar’ı canlandıran Lizge Cömert, dünyanın küresel ısınmaya çare aradığı bir zirvede buluştu. Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) İklim Değişikliği Konferansı COP31’de bir araya gelen iki kadın sanatçı, Metin Erksan imzalı Susuz Yaz’ın özel gösterimi ve söyleşisinde buluştu.
Etkinlik için Susuz Yaz’ın çekimlerinin devam ettiği Adana’dan Antalya’ya gelen Lizge Cömert, Hülya Koçyiğit ile birlikte “Susuz Yaz” afişinin önünde poz verdi. Usta oyuncu, Lizge Cömert’in elini tutarken “Hülya Koçyiğit el verdi.” diyerek halefine tam desteğini gösterdi.
Susuz Yaz’ın gerçek olaylardan esinlendiğini vurgulayan Hülya Koçyiğit, “İzmir Urla'daki Bademler Köyü'nde geçiyor. Gerçek karakterleri canlandırdık. Su bir kişinin olamaz, bunun hikayesiydi." dedi.
Koçyiğit, iklim değişikliğiyle mücadelede herkese sorumluluk düştüğünü söyleyerek, “İyi ki böyle bir organizasyon yapıldı. Çünkü dünyayı ne yazık ki çok hor kullandık. Ardı ardına felaketler yaşıyoruz. Bu, giderek dünyayı tükettiğimizi gösteriyor. " diye konuştu.
Susuz Yaz’ın Kanal D ekranında ‘yeni dizi’ olarak hayat bulacak olmasından duyduğu mutluluğu dile getiren Koçyiğit, “Kanal D'de yakında yayınlanmaya başlayacak Susuz Yaz dizisi beni çok heyecanlandırdı. Ben de baştan sona izleyeceğim. Merakla bekliyorum. " dedi.
Kanal D 'nin Ay Yapım imzalı yeni dizisi 'Susuz Yaz'da Bahar karakterine hayat veren Lizge Cömert ise usta oyuncuya duyduğu hayranlığı dile getirerek, “Ortak bir hikayeyi farklı şekilde yorumlayacağız. Çok heyecanlıyım." ifadelerini kullandı.
Senaryosunu Sema Ergenekon'un kaleme aldığı Ay Yapım imzalı Susuz Yaz dizisinin çekimleri Adana'da sürüyor. Hikayesi 1970'li yılların Çarlak Köyü'nde geçen yapımda Osman karakterini Mert Ramazan Demir, Bahar'ı Lizge Cömert ve Hasan'ı ise Batuhan Bozkurt Yüzgüleç canlandırıyor.

Tekirdağ'da sosyal medya üzerinden tanıştığı Bulgaristan'da yaşayan bir kadınla evlenmek isteyen yaşlı yurttaş, dolandırıcılık ve şantaj şebekesinin hedefi oldu.
Yurttaşın şikâyeti üzerine Tekirdağ Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı koordinesinde İl Emniyet Müdürlüğü Asayiş Şube Müdürlüğü ekipleri tarafından soruşturma başlatıldı.
Yapılan incelemelerde, şüphelilerin kendilerini polis olarak tanıtarak yurttaşı korku ve baskıyla para göndermeye yönlendirdikleri belirlendi.
Soruşturmaya göre şüpheliler, yaşlı yurttaşa evlenmek istediği kadının uluslararası kara para aklama, terör örgütleri ve dolandırıcılık suçlarına karıştığını söyledi.
Gizli bir operasyon yürütüldüğünü öne süren şüpheliler, yurttaşın da bu operasyona destek vermesi gerektiğini belirterek kendisini para göndermeye ikna etti.
Şüphelilerin, şantaj ve çeşitli vaatlerle yönlendirdikleri yurttaşa farklı IBAN hesaplarına toplam 1 milyon 914 bin TL gönderttikleri tespit edildi.
Soruşturmanın genişletilmesiyle birlikte şüphelilere ait banka hesapları incelemeye alındı.
Yapılan mali incelemelerde, dolandırıcılık suçları kapsamında toplam 724 milyon TL'lik finansal işlem hacmi belirlendi.
Suçtan elde edildiği değerlendirilen paraların kripto varlıklar ve farklı soğuk cüzdan hesapları aracılığıyla yurt dışına aktarıldığı tespit edildi.
Şüphelilerin yakalanması amacıyla 9 Kasım 2026 tarihinde 15 ilde eş zamanlı operasyon düzenlendi.
Operasyonlarda 23 şüpheli yakalanarak gözaltına alındı. Şüphelilerin üzerlerinde, evlerinde ve işyerlerinde gerçekleştirilen aramalarda suçta kullanıldığı değerlendirilen çok sayıda dijital materyal ve belgeye el konuldu.
Emniyetteki işlemlerinin ardından adliyeye sevk edilen şüphelilerden 6'sı nitelikli dolandırıcılık ve şantaj suçlarından tutuklandı. Diğer 17 şüpheli ise adli kontrol şartıyla serbest bırakıldı.
Yetkililer, evlilik, yatırım ve yüksek kazanç vaadiyle gerçekleştirilen dolandırıcılık girişimlerine karşı yurttaşları uyardı.
Kendilerini polis, savcı veya başka bir kamu görevlisi olarak tanıtarak para talep eden kişilere kesinlikle itibar edilmemesi gerektiği vurgulandı.
